triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: In brief, the energy of sunlight is “captured” to energize electrons, whose energy is then stored in the covalent bonds of sugar molecules.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: It is the only biological process that can capture energy that originates from sunlight and convert it into chemical compounds (carbohydrates) that every organism uses to power its metabolism.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: It is also a source of oxygen necessary for many living organisms.

triples.head: Plants
triples.evidence: Plants, algae, and a group of bacteria called cyanobacteria are the only organisms capable of performing photosynthesis.

triples.head: Algae

triples.head: Cyanobacteria
triples.evidence: Plants, algae, and a group of bacteria called cyanobacteria are the only organisms capable of performing photosynthesis.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: Photosynthesis is a multi-step process that requires specific wavelengths of visible sunlight, carbon dioxide (which is low in energy), and water as substrates.

triples.head: Photosynthesis

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: After the process is complete, it releases oxygen and produces glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P), as well as simple carbohydrate molecules (high in energy) that can then be converted into glucose, sucrose, or any of dozens of other sugar molecules.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: In plants, photosynthesis generally takes place in leaves, which consist of several layers of cells.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: The process of photosynthesis occurs in a middle layer called the mesophyll.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: In all autotrophic eukaryotes, photosynthesis takes place inside an organelle called a chloroplast.

triples.head: Chloroplast
triples.evidence: Within the chloroplast are stacked, disc-shaped structures called thylakoids.

triples.head: Thylakoid
triples.evidence: Embedded in the thylakoid membrane is chlorophyll, a pigment (molecule that absorbs light) responsible for the initial interaction between light and plant material, and numerous proteins that make up the electron transport chain.

triples.head: Photosynthesis
triples.evidence: Photosynthesis takes place in two sequential stages: the light-dependent reactions and the light-independent reactions.

triples.head: Photosynthesis

triples.head: Light-dependent reactions
triples.evidence: The light-dependent reactions utilize certain molecules to temporarily store the energy: These are referred to as energy carriers.

triples.head: Light-independent reactions
triples.evidence: The Calvin cycle, which takes place in the stroma, uses energy derived from these compounds to make G3P from CO2.
